capabilities: Show daily notes on a monthly calendar with photo covers, mood markers and weather icons
Search and filter a journal timeline by date range, source, mood, favorite, location, tag and media type
Record five-level moods with notes and labels, then review trends and reports
Fetch current and historical weather for dates from Open-Meteo
Resurface past entries and photos through an On This Day panel
disambiguation: Not a journaling editor with its own entry format; it indexes existing Markdown daily notes and leaves their bodies as they are.
extras: Mood records are stored in a separate JSON file (default Calendar/journal-metadata.json) with optional frontmatter mirroring; weather needs no API key; EXIF GPS reverse geocoding is off until enabled; HEIC/HEIF thumbnail conversion runs on desktop only.
intentEvidence: It runs on Obsidian desktop and mobile, and is built for vaults that already use Daily Notes.
problem: Daily notes are plain files with no visual way to browse them by date, mood, weather or media, and users do not want their notes moved or rewritten.

relations.evidence: Dayline migrates settings from an earlier dayline installation or Calendar Sidebar 1.x.
create the missing note from your Daily Notes template (Templater supported)

summary: Visual journal that turns a folder of Markdown daily notes into a calendar and searchable timeline with mood, weather, photos and On This Day memories.
